history.origins: Vitou is a traditional card game from Nice, France (Niçois/Provençal heritage). It is also played in Piedmont, the Provence Alps, and under various guises in Lombardy, Friuli, and Suisse Romande. It is closely related to the Catalan game Truc but was adapted to the French 32-card Belote deck; the 10s and 9s substitute for the missing low cards, giving the game its distinctive ranking (10, 9, Ace high). The rules documented for this game derive from information provided by Nicolas Morlino.
timeline: Traditional: Niçois game from Nice, France; closely related to Catalan Truc, adapted to the French 32-card deck (Belote style).
history.cultural: Provençal and Niçois gaming heritage; also played in Piedmont, Lombardy, Friuli, and Suisse Romande.
history.evolution: Related to Catalan Truc; adapted from Truc to the French 32-card deck used for Belote, with 10s and 9s taking the role of the highest cards.

setup.dealing: 3 cards each, clockwise. First dealer: lowest card from draw.

rules.objective: Win rounds by taking best two of three tricks; first team to 21 points wins the game.
